name: Question 18
worked_solution:
First, we note that 

$$
F(t)=\int {F}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t=\int ⟨\operatorname{tan}⁡t\operatorname{sec}⁡t\,,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩\text{d}t.
$$

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨\operatorname{tan}⁡t\operatorname{sec}⁡t\,,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩\text{d}t & =⟨\int \operatorname{tan}⁡t\operatorname{sec}⁡t\,\text{d}t,\int 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡t+{c}_{1},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+{c}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The initial condition $F(\pi )=⟨-3,\,3⟩$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}F(\pi )=⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡(\pi )+{c}_{1},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )+{c}_{2}⟩ & =⟨-3,\,3⟩ \\ ⟨-1+{c}_{1},\,{c}_{2}⟩ & =⟨-3,\,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${c}_{1}=-2$ and ${c}_{2}=3.$ Consequently

$$
F(t)=⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡t-2,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+3⟩.
$$

Question 18

If F′(t)=⟨tan⁡tsec⁡t,2cos⁡(2t)⟩ and F(π)=⟨−3,3⟩, then F(t)=

a
 ⟨sec2⁡t−3,sin⁡(3t)−2⟩
b
 ⟨sec⁡t−2,sin⁡(t)+3⟩
c
⟨sec⁡t−2,sin⁡(2t)+3⟩
d
 ⟨sec⁡(2t)−2,sin⁡(2t)+3⟩
e
⟨sec⁡t+3,sin⁡(2t)−2⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we note that

F(t)=∫F′(t)dt=∫⟨tan⁡tsec⁡t,2cos⁡(2t)⟩dt.

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we have

∫⟨tan⁡tsec⁡t,2cos⁡(2t)⟩dt=⟨∫tan⁡tsec⁡tdt,∫2cos⁡(2t)dt⟩=⟨sec⁡t+c1,sin⁡(2t)+c2⟩.

The initial condition F(π)=⟨−3,3⟩ gives

F(π)=⟨sec⁡(π)+c1,sin⁡(2π)+c2⟩=⟨−3,3⟩⟨−1+c1,c2⟩=⟨−3,3⟩.

Therefore, c1=−2 and c2=3. Consequently

F(t)=⟨sec⁡t−2,sin⁡(2t)+3⟩.
